method: WebSearch for discovery across multiple query angles (foreign aerospace/defence India investment, plant announcements, JVs, MRO expansions, company-specific follow-ups), followed by WebFetch to open and read each candidate source directly before inclusion. Every finding below was verified by opening at least one substantive article/press release via WebFetch (not a search snippet alone); where the primary company press release could not be fetched (blocked/403), a trade-press article quoting the company directly was used instead and is noted. Non-Indian-HQ companies only. Session's WebSearch quota was exhausted after ~19 queries, which capped a few further discovery angles (Elbit Systems recency check, additional confirmation attempt for a Diehl Defence lead) rather than any change in method or standards -- those items are recorded honestly in negative_notes rather than included on an unverified basis.

findings.signal: Signed a Joint Venture Cooperation Agreement with Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) on 24 Nov 2025 to incorporate a 50:50 India joint venture that will localise manufacturing, supply and maintenance of the HAMMER precision-guided air-to-ground weapon system for the Indian Air Force and Navy, targeting ~60% indigenisation over time.

Inaugurated the world's largest LEAP engine (CFM International) maintenance, repair and overhaul centre in Hyderabad, a EUR 200 million-plus investment, to reduce overseas MRO dependence for Indian carriers (IndiGo, Air India) and serve civil and military programmes; company stated it plans to triple annual revenue from Indian operations by decade end.

First defence-sector project in India approved under the 100% FDI route: Saab's plant in Jhajjar, Haryana will manufacture the Carl-Gustaf shoulder-fired weapon system (Saab's first Carl-Gustaf plant outside Sweden) for Indian forces and export, with manufacturing due to begin once the industrial licence is granted -- confirmed on record by Mats Palmberg, Saab's Chairman and Managing Director in India.

Announced a fresh Rs 100 crore investment in its Pune manufacturing facility (welding technologies, inspection equipment, precision tooling), bringing total investment at the site to Rs 510 crore over three years; the facility produces components for GE90/GEnx/GE9X and CFM LEAP commercial engines and works with 300+ local suppliers.

Developing a new Defence Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul facility in Bangalore jointly with Tata Advanced Systems, scheduled to be operational in early 2027, alongside a proposal to the Indian Air Force to establish a C-130J Super Hercules final assembly line in India -- what would be Lockheed's first such line outside the US.

Opened the Collins India Operations Center, a new 26-acre 'Factory of the Future' manufacturing site at KIADB Aerospace Park, Bengaluru, initially producing seats, lighting and cargo systems, temperature sensors, communication/navigation systems, water solutions and evacuation slides; expected to host 2,200+ employees by 2026.

Entered a long-term licensing and technology-transfer partnership with JSW Defence for a USD 90 million unmanned-aerial-systems manufacturing facility at EMC Maheshwaram, Hyderabad, to produce Shield AI's V-BAT Group 3 drone for the Indian armed forces and export; foundation stone laid 2 Dec 2025, manufacturing targeted for Q4 2026.

Disclosed plans to invest Rs 3,000 crore in India's defence sector for military-systems manufacturing, with Haryana shortlisted as one of seven potential sites nationally (no location finalised yet); disclosed by IAI's India-arm chief of staff during a meeting with Haryana's Chief Minister.

Launched ELTX, a joint venture with India's DCX Systems Limited, to develop and localise production and maintenance of high-end airborne radars and ground-based defence systems in India, as part of deepening Israel-India defence-technology transfer.

Signed four Production Transfer Agreements with Tata Advanced Systems Limited to manufacture Rafale fighter-jet fuselage sections (lateral shells, rear/central/front sections) at a new plant in Hyderabad -- the first-ever Rafale fuselage production outside France -- with production starting FY2028 at up to two complete fuselages per month.

Established a fully-owned Indian subsidiary with a corporate office in AeroCity, New Delhi, to build out teams across defence, commercial aviation, business aviation, services & support and urban air mobility, calling India 'a key market'; follows a Feb 2024 MoU with Mahindra Defence on the C-390 medium transport aircraft.

Struck a strategic partnership with India's Reliance Defence for large-scale ammunition manufacturing (up to 200,000 artillery shells, 10,000 tons of explosives, 2,000 tons of propellants annually) at a new Reliance-built plant in the Watad industrial area, Maharashtra; on-record CEO quote calling it 'a strong commitment to partner with India.'

findings.signal: First domestically-assembled C-295 military transport aircraft rolled out (months ahead of schedule) from the Tata Advanced Systems-Airbus final assembly line in Vadodara -- the first time a private-sector facility has produced a military aircraft in India; 40 of the 56-aircraft IAF order will be built at Vadodara through 2031, with 85%+ structural/final assembly done locally.

negative_notes.reason_excluded: Real and large (Rs 6,000 crore, Devanahalli, Karnataka) announced integrated aerospace/defence/semiconductor hub, but AxisCades is headquartered in Bengaluru, India -- excluded per the task's instruction to cover only non-India-headquartered companies.

A WebSearch snippet (Business Standard) described Diehl partnering with Reliance Defence to produce terminally guided munitions at the same Watad/Ratnagiri site as the verified Rheinmetall deal (~Rs 5,000 crore over five years). The Business Standard article returned HTTP 403 on WebFetch and no alternate primary source could be located and opened before the session's search quota ran out, so this lead could not be independently read and verified. Left out per this sweep's rule that every finding must be backed by an article actually opened via WebFetch -- worth re-checking in a future pass.

negative_notes.company: Kalyani Rafael Advanced Systems (Rafael Advanced Defense Systems, Israel)
negative_notes.reason_excluded: Genuine, substantial JV (Kalyani Strategic Systems + Rafael) manufacturing Spike anti-tank missiles in Hyderabad, but the facility was inaugurated in 2017. No new 2025-2026 investment, expansion, or capacity announcement for this JV was found in this sweep -- excluded as stale/pre-existing rather than new activity, per the task's instruction not to re-report long-standing operations without fresh news.

Existing Hermes 450/900 drone supply relationship with India (in IAF service for years) surfaced repeatedly, plus an unrelated Jan 2026 item about Elbit buying out Thales' stake in the UAV Tactical Systems JV that does not appear to be India-specific. No substantive NEW 2025-2026 India investment, plant, or JV announcement for Elbit was found before the session's WebSearch quota was exhausted -- flagged as an angle worth a follow-up sweep rather than confirmed absent.

The only substantive 'Bell helicopter plant in India' article found (IBEF) is dated 16 March 2016 and describes an exploratory feasibility study targeting 2018-19 operation -- a decade-old, apparently unrealized plan. No 2025-2026 confirmation or update was found; excluded as stale, not a current signal.

Boeing's India coverage in the window is broad relationship/vision language (largest foreign OEM sourcing from India at $1.25bn/year, ~$100m historical pilot-training investment, a Liquid Robotics-Sagar Defence Engineering MoU on autonomous surface vessels) rather than one specific, dated, dollar-figured NEW capital commitment that could be independently opened and verified via WebFetch within the research budget available. Excluded from findings for lack of a single crisp, verified investment signal -- not because Boeing lacks India activity, but because nothing surfaced met this sweep's bar for a substantive, individually-verified announcement.
